# OpenMajiang client integration guide

This document describes public client interfaces. It provides no operator
credentials, hidden-card channel, arbitrary Bot-code hosting or scoring override.
The exact current HTTP contract is /openapi.json. Wire schemas are published at
/schemas/dto.json, /schemas/protocol.json, /schemas/ws-client.json,
/schemas/ws-server.json and /schemas/spectator.json.

## Accounts

Register with POST /v1/auth/register {email,password,name,accept_terms:true}.
Passwords contain 15–128 Unicode characters; preserve spaces. The generic 202
response means an eligible email request was queued, not that SMTP delivered it.
Existing addresses receive the same unauthenticated response. A registration
does not yet authorize joining a table.

Verification and reset links place their one-time token in the URL fragment.
GET displays a confirmation page. POST /v1/auth/verify-email {token} consumes a
verification token; POST /v1/auth/reset-password {token,password} consumes a
reset token and revokes old human sessions. Do not put fragments, request bodies,
cookies, passwords or bearer credentials in logs or analytics.

POST /v1/auth/login {email,password} sets an HttpOnly SameSite session cookie and
returns {user,csrf_token}. GET /v1/me returns the same private identity and CSRF
token. Browser writes require the exact configured Origin and, after login,
X-CSRF-Token. Cookie credentials must not be copied into localStorage. Account
data includes private email, role and status; public display names use distinct
public DTOs. An unverified account may watch and manage its verification process,
but cannot join games or manage Bots.

The account supports display-name changes, devices, logout, password change,
new-email confirmation, delivery status and account deletion. Sensitive changes
verify current credentials. Password/email changes revoke old human sessions;
Bot runtime credentials are independently revoked through their own endpoints.
Deletion revokes both kinds and anonymizes personal identity while retaining
stable match references. No API lets a registrant assign themselves operator.

## Discover rules and rooms

GET /v1/rulesets returns versioned manifests: seat counts, formats, online
profiles, plugin API, state/view schema, renderer and artifact fingerprint.
artifact_hash identifies the running compiled executable; source_hash records
the source digest, and build records Go version, OS and architecture. Preserve
these identities when reproducing a match; a source digest alone is not binary
compatibility evidence for a compiled ruleset.
Room creation fixes a ruleset/version/profile/format. The server rejects invalid
combinations. The first MCR plugin uses 144 tiles, 81 scoring patterns and an
8-point nonflower eligibility threshold. The rule evaluator, legal options and
final server settlement are authoritative; an SDK must not compute and submit
its own replacement score.

GET /v1/public/rooms discovers all tables. POST /v1/rooms creates a table;
POST /v1/rooms/{id}/join requests a seat. An invitation controls admission only:
every table remains anonymously viewable. Waiting-room ownership permits
configuration, invite rotation and eligible Bot additions, not hidden-card
access or in-game manipulation. Public queue matching never silently fills a
human-only table with Bots. Self-test rooms require invite admission and remain
outside comparable public Bot statistics.

Room participant identities are stable. Physical seat assignment may change
between hands or rounds. Use participant_id together with current seat_id,
hand_id, seat_assignment_version and control_epoch. Never authorize a player
from the room owner field, a former seat or a remembered seat number alone.

## Human control

GET /v1/rooms/{id}/view returns an authorized private snapshot. A new tab may be
read-only while another tab holds the control lease. POST /v1/rooms/{id}/take-control
explicitly claims control and returns control_token and the new control_epoch.
Human HTTP actions send that token as X-Control-Token in addition to session,
Origin and CSRF. Never use a CSRF token or user ID as a substitute controller.

The player WebSocket is /v1/ws/players?room_id=... and uses the browser cookie.
After an HTTP takeover a tab may send {type:"resume_control",control_token:...}
to bind its existing socket to that lease. control_readonly is not an actionable
grant; control_granted carries the current token and epoch. A replaced old
controller receives control_changed and must stop, rather than auto-steal control.

## Self-hosted Bots

A verified owner creates a Bot through POST /v1/bots, records immutable strategy
versions and issues a credential through POST /v1/bots/{id}/credentials. The
api_key is returned only once. Keep strategy code and any LLM API keys on the
owner's machine. The platform does not receive arbitrary executable source.

Exchange a long key through POST /v1/bot-sessions, Authorization: Bearer LONG_KEY,
with {protocol_version:"1.0",rulesets:[{id,version},...]}. The result includes a
30-minute session_token. Use that short token for GET /v1/bot/active-match,
POST/DELETE /v1/bot/queue and the Bot WSS Authorization header. Keys and sessions
must never appear in query strings. TLS certificate verification is mandatory
for remote connections.

Connect to /v1/ws/bots?room_id=...; omitting room_id discovers the Bot's own active
seat. Send {type:"ready"} after a waiting room_snapshot. When all publicly matched
seats confirm, the server starts the match. Capability declarations must include
the exact room ruleset version. After a terminal match, close the room-specific
socket and discover the next active room. continuous queues do not move an old
socket to a new room automatically. Refresh short sessions before expiry.

GET /v1/bots/{id}/status is an owner-only runtime panel: authenticated presence,
connected seat lease, active_room_id, active_match_id, queued, continuous and up
to 20 recent errors. Only error codes and timestamps are retained in this panel.

## Decisions and observations

The server sends a full snapshot followed by decision_request. The decision's
observation_ref must exactly match the snapshot's stream_id and view_seq. Match,
hand, participant, seat assignment and control epoch must also match. A decision
sequence number follows the snapshot, while command_ack, command_error,
heartbeat, seat_assigned and other control messages are not observation updates.
Do not use a receipt as a replacement private snapshot.

New hands start with seat_assigned and a new stream. A missing state or mismatched
observation requires {type:"resume"}; wait for a fresh snapshot before invoking
strategy. REST private snapshots contain their decision atomically; the
observation_ref fields specifically describe the WebSocket snapshot barrier.

Only use the legal_actions in that decision. submit_action includes type,
protocol_version, match_id, hand_id, participant_id, seat_id,
seat_assignment_version, control_epoch, decision_id, window_id, command_id and
option_id. Generate a fresh 8–128-character command_id for a new decision. On
lost ACK, retry the entire identical command with that same ID and payload.
Changing payload under an existing ID is IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT.

An ACK status of recorded means the response was durably locked, not that a
chi/pong/kong won adjudication. Response windows keep a fixed deadline and all
eligible responders retain their original opportunities. Use the later snapshot
as the result. applied denotes an immediately adjudicated direct action.

Cancel strategy when a new snapshot, hand or control epoch supersedes it. Measure
server_time/deadline_at with a local budget and network safety margin. Never
submit a late inference result. The SDK silently returns the sole pass option
without calling strategy. Automatic flower replacement is a configurable SDK
preference; it does not modify the server's legal action list or rule version.

Reconnect with jittered backoff, authenticate again if necessary, then restore
the snapshot barrier. The recorded field can carry an already accepted decision
receipt. The server looks up recorded idempotent commands after authentication
but before current deadline/lease checks. This makes an identical old-command
retry safe without authorizing a new stale command. Self/reaction timeout counts
are visible only in the owning participant snapshot for integration diagnostics.

## Anonymous discard-only spectators

Anyone may GET /v1/public/rooms/{id}/spectator and public replay endpoints.
For WSS, POST /v1/public/rooms/{id}/spectator-ticket, connect to
/v1/ws/spectators?room_id=..., and send {type:"authenticate",ticket:...} within
5 seconds. No table data is sent before ticket authentication. It is read-only.

The public view is spectator_discard_only@1. Its only card-face path is
view.discards[].kind (replay frames have the same view projection). It includes
an independent discard_id and claimed flag, never the physical tile entity ID.
No concealed hands, flower faces, meld faces, winning hand, winning tile, scoring
pattern explanations, wall order or entropy seed may appear. The restriction
continues at hand end, match end and in all public replay pages. A logged-in
owner or participant querying a public endpoint still receives this projection.

Public non-card metadata may show identities, player kinds, seat/round winds,
hand counts, remaining-wall count, action names, scores and termination method.
Do not infer missing private information by requesting another seat_id. Private
history requires the explicit owner/participant endpoint and, for a Bot,
authorized bot_id selection.

## Replay, statistics and errors

Replay pages return frames,next_after,view_policy. Request after=next_after with
limit<=200 until frames is empty; hand_index can filter one hand. HTTP private
history and public discard-only history remain separate audiences.

GET /v1/public/matches and /v1/me/matches accept mode, ruleset_id,
ruleset_version, match_format, status and bot_id filters. Pagination uses the
opaque next_before value as before; limit defaults to 25 and is capped at 100.
Private Bot history selects an explicitly owned bot_id. After 30 days, terminal
card-bearing snapshots and replays return 410 MATCH_ARCHIVED; public match
details retain only typed settled-score summaries and the archive timestamp.

Statistics use settled-facts@1. Compare only matching ruleset, version, profile,
format, clock, mode, configuration hash, Bot version and queue pool. Metrics have
value:number|null and samples; no samples means null, never invented zero.
Incomplete, self-test, interrupted or trustee-assisted cohorts are not comparable
competitive results. Raw participant-hand samples are not physical hand counts.

AUTH_EXPIRED requires authentication; STALE_CONTROL requires stopping the old
controller; DECISION_CLOSED requires a current snapshot; ALREADY_SUBMITTED means
wait for resolution. INVALID_OPTION may be corrected only while the original
deadline remains open. IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT cannot be blindly retried with another
payload. Rate limits and slow-consumer disconnections protect service capacity.
Server errors never expand a caller's identity or hidden-card audience.
